what: The DID Approach - Using Late Cohort as Control
title: NTD-identification
text: uses trend late cohort impute counterfactual early cohort:  green line (imputed counterfactual) doesn’t match light blue line (true counterfactual). difference bias due parallel trend violations. happens late cohort steeper slope counterfactual earnings.
code: # Calculate DID-imputed counterfactual did_cf <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 0), function(g) {   # Early cohort's pre-treatment level   early_pre <- data %>%     filter(female == g, D == d_early, age == d_early - 1) %>%     pull(y)      # Late cohort trend   late_cf <- data %>% filter(female == g, D == d_late) %>% select(age, y_0)   late_pre <- late_cf %>% filter(age == d_early - 1) %>% pull(y_0)      # DID imputation: shift late trend to match early pre-treatment level   tibble(     age    = late_cf$age,     female = g,     D      = d_early,     series = "y_cf_did",     value  = early_pre + (late_cf$y_0 - late_pre)   ) })) %>%   mutate(     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men")),     cohort = factor("Early (D=25)", levels = c("Early (D=25)", "Late (D=30)")),     series_label = "Early — DID-imputed CF",     linetype = "dotdash",     color = "CF DID"   )  plot_df_plus <- bind_rows(plot_df, did_cf)  ggplot(plot_df_plus, aes(x = age, y = value, group = series_label)) +   geom_line(aes(linetype = linetype, color = color), linewidth = 1.1) +   facet_wrap(~ gender, nrow = 1) +   scale_linetype_identity() +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(       "Obs." = "#1f77b4", "CF Early" = "#9ecae1",        "CF Late" = "#fdae6b", "CF DID" = "#2ca02c"     )   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 2: DID-Imputed Counterfactual",     subtitle = "Green line = what DID thinks would have happened without treatment",     x = "Age", y = "Earnings", color = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: aggregate-estimands
text: multiple_treatment_group_analysis() estimates child-penalty effects separately treatment group dd (age first birth). groups differ baseline earnings, age composition, selection, single group’s estimate directly comparable another’s. aggregate_estimands() collapses group-specific estimates single number per event time, answering question: average effect across distribution first-birth ages? Three aggregate estimands available: avg_of_ratios (θAgg,1\theta_{\text{Agg},1}): weighted average group’s normalized effect θ(g,d,d+e)\theta(g,d,d+e). Formally, θAgg,1(g,e)=∑dwd⋅θ(g,d,d+e)\theta_{\text{Agg},1}(g,e) = \sum_d w_d \cdot \theta(g,d,d+e), wdw_d population weights normalised sum one. Preferred normalization happens within group aggregation, baseline differences inflate average. ratio_of_avgs (θAgg,2\theta_{\text{Agg},2}): ratio weighted-average ATE weighted-average APO. Formally, θAgg,2(g,e)=∑dwd⋅ATE(g,d,d+e)/∑dwd⋅APO(g,d,d+e)\theta_{\text{Agg},2}(g,e) = \sum_d w_d \cdot \text{ATE}(g,d,d+e) \;/\; \sum_d w_d \cdot \text{APO}(g,d,d+e). implicitly -weights high-earning groups (larger APO contributes proportionally pooled denominator), differs θAgg,1\theta_{\text{Agg},1} earnings vary across groups. gender_ineq (ΔρAgg\Delta\rho_{\text{Agg}}): weighted average NTD_New theta estimates — aggregate gender-inequality penalty. Formally, ΔρAgg(e)=∑dwd⋅Δρ(d,d+e)\Delta\rho_{\text{Agg}}(e) = \sum_d w_d \cdot \Delta\rho(d,d+e).

text: Let \(Y(, g, d^\star)\) denote mean outcome age \(\) gender \(g \\{0,1\}\) (1 = female) assigned group \(d^\star\). core components : APO(g; d, d', ) \(= Y(d-\mathrm{pre}, g, d) + Y(, g, d') - Y(d-\mathrm{pre}, g, d')\) ATE(g; d, d', ) \(= Y(, g, d) - \mathrm{APO}(g; d, d', )\) \(\theta\)(g) \(= \mathrm{ATE}(g) / \mathrm{APO}(g)\) , cross-gender contrasts formed: TD \(= \mathrm{ATE}(F) - \mathrm{ATE}(M)\) NTD_Conv \(= \theta(F) - \theta(M)\) NTD_New \(= \frac{Y(,F,d)}{Y(,M,d)} - \frac{\mathrm{APO}(F)}{\mathrm{APO}(M)}\) TD Null NTD_Conv_Null variants defined analogously null-effect--fathers bias-correction. Internally, influence functions pieces written temporary columns data.table via compute_mean_if(), cluster-robust standard errors computed summing IFs id level via se_cluster().
